title: NEB Class 12 Mathematics — Differentiation — 2024
subject: mathematics
source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Differentiate: (a) y = x³ tan x, (b) y = ln(sinx).
questions.solution:
**(a)** product rule: dy/dx = 3x²·tan x + x³·sec²x = **x²(3 tan x + x sec²x)**.

**(b)** chain rule: dy/dx = (1/sinx)·cosx = **cot x** (valid for sinx > 0).

State the rule used for each: product rule for (a), chain rule for (b).
questions.knowledgeNote: With more than two factors, differentiate one factor at a time and add the terms — the same rule extends to a triple product.

questions.question: If y = √(1 + x²), prove that (1 + x²)y″ + x y′ = y.
questions.solution:
y² = 1 + x², so differentiating: 2y y′ = 2x → y′ = x/y.

Differentiate again: y″ = (y·1 − x·y′)/y² = (y − x·(x/y))/y² = (y² − x²)/y³.

Since y² − x² = 1, we get y″ = 1/y³.

Now (1 + x²)y″ + x y′ = y²·(1/y³) + x·(x/y) = 1/y + x²/y = (1 + x²)/y = y²/y = **y**, as required.
questions.knowledgeNote: This style of proof (square first, differentiate implicitly) avoids ugly square roots in the second derivative — always look for it.

questions.question: Find dy/dx if x = a(θ − sin θ) and y = a(1 − cos θ).
questions.solution:
dx/dθ = a(1 − cosθ), dy/dθ = a sinθ.

dy/dx = (dy/dθ)/(dx/dθ) = a sinθ / a(1 − cosθ) = sinθ/(1 − cosθ).

Using the half-angle identities: = [2 sin(θ/2)cos(θ/2)]/[2 sin²(θ/2)] = **cot(θ/2)**. At θ = π/2 the slope is cot(π/4) = 1.
questions.knowledgeNote: For parametric curves always divide the derivatives, and simplify with half-angle identities — the cycloid slope simplification is a standard question.
